policy: Employees must badge individually into restricted areas and may not admit another person using their credentials.
Restricted areas require employee badges and, where appropriate, biometric verification and a personal identification number.
High-value areas, including AI model laboratories, require two-person entry where designated.
Lobby doors must close automatically after entry, and security personnel must monitor entrances to prevent tailgating.
Physical Access.risk: Piggybacking, tailgating, badge cloning, and unauthorized physical access
Physical Access.controls: Badge readers, biometric scanners, PIN verification, smart gate mantraps, automatic door closing, restricted access zones, and security monitoring

policy: Visitors must be registered in advance, verify their identity, receive temporary identification, and remain in approved areas.
Visitors must be escorted whenever they enter restricted zones.
Reception must record visitor entry and exit, and visitor records must be retained for one year.
Visitor access must not provide access to source code, AI models, production servers, or other restricted systems.
Visitors and Vendors.risk: Unauthorized physical access, social engineering, and exposure of confidential company information
Visitors and Vendors.controls: Visitor management system, reception identity verification, temporary badges, escorts, access restrictions, and visitor logs

policy: Employees must lock their workstations whenever unattended.
All employee endpoints must automatically lock after three minutes of inactivity.
Privacy filters are mandatory for workstations in open areas and locations where screens may be visible to unauthorized people.
Employees must not leave source code, customer data, AI research, or other sensitive information exposed.
Workstation Security.risk: Piggybacking, shoulder surfing, unattended workstation access, and confidential information exposure
Workstation Security.controls: Automatic screen locks, employee awareness training, privacy filters, workstation positioning, and restricted-area access

policy: Lumina Systems requires unique user credentials and MFA for internal systems.
Hardware security keys using FIDO2/WebAuthn must be used where supported by the authentication system.
Role-based access control (RBAC), least privilege, and need-to-know principles determine resource access.
Access to source code, AI models, production servers, and administrative consoles must be limited to authorized roles.
Privilege escalation requires manager approval and must be recorded by the security monitoring system.
Access badges must be combined with biometric verification and a PIN at designated high-security checkpoints.
Authentication and Authorization.risk: Unauthorized digital access, credential theft, privilege abuse, and physical access badge cloning
Authentication and Authorization.controls: MFA, FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys, RBAC, least privilege, biometric verification, PINs, access reviews, and audit logs

policy: Unapproved removable media is prohibited on restricted systems.
USB ports must be disabled or restricted where business needs do not require removable media.
Exceptions require explicit authorization from the security team and must be logged.
Approved devices must undergo malware scanning before use.
Sensitive data must not be copied to removable storage without documented authorization.
Removable Media.risk: Malware introduction, unauthorized data transfer, and exposure of proprietary source code or customer data
Removable Media.controls: USB port restrictions, endpoint protection, malware scanning, approval procedures, device monitoring, and access logging

policy: Sensitive paper documents must be placed in approved, locked destruction containers and must never enter ordinary trash.
Packaging and labels that reveal company purchases, equipment details, serial numbers, or internal operations must be destroyed or securely removed before disposal.
Electronic storage devices must be securely erased or physically destroyed according to their sensitivity.
Document Disposal.risk: Dumpster diving, information disclosure, and exposure of equipment or operational details
Document Disposal.controls: Locked destruction bins, secure shredding, label removal, approved electronic media destruction, and clean-desk procedures

policy: Critical computing systems must use UPS and surge protection.
Selected critical services must receive generator support and have documented recovery procedures.
Critical data and configurations must be backed up regularly, and recovery procedures must be tested.
The company must inspect vulnerable power infrastructure and prioritize resilience measures in high-risk areas.
Power disruptions affecting AI training, production servers, or customer services must be reported and investigated.
Power and Continuity.risk: Power outages, extreme weather, flooding, equipment damage, and disruption of critical AI services
Power and Continuity.controls: UPS, surge protection, generator support, backups, recovery testing, infrastructure inspections, and environmental monitoring

policy: IP cameras must use strong, unique passwords and MFA where supported.
Camera firmware must be updated and unsupported devices must be replaced or isolated.
Security logs must be forwarded to a secured, centralized logging platform.
Logs must use tamper-resistant storage, such as WORM storage, with access limited to authorized personnel.
Suspicious changes to camera configurations, missing footage, and unexpected log modifications must be investigated.
Security Logs and Camera Protection.risk: Tampered security logs, compromised IP cameras, false security records, and concealed physical intrusions
Security Logs and Camera Protection.controls: MFA, strong passwords, firmware updates, network segmentation, centralized SIEM logging, WORM storage, and monitoring

policy: Employees must promptly report suspicious activity, unauthorized access attempts, and lost access badges.
Security events must be recorded and evaluated using documented detection rules.
Repeated failed access attempts, badge and biometric mismatches, and unusual source code transfers must trigger investigation when established alert thresholds are met.
Alerts must be investigated before a confirmed-incident decision is made.
Investigators must distinguish observed evidence from assumptions about compromise or malicious intent.
Monitoring and Reporting.risk: Delayed attack detection, inaccurate security records, undetected unauthorized access, and false-positive alerts
Monitoring and Reporting.controls: Centralized SIEM, tamper-resistant logs, CCTV, badge records, automated detection rules, incident investigation, and employee reporting
